findings.title: Saved-project lifecycle and save-quota enforcement are mis-modeled
findings.detail: The tasks create a `project_id` and persist `source.png` during `/api/upload`, then gate free save quota at upload time (`11.3`). That conflicts with the spec/proposal, which treat save quota as applying to saved projects, require failed generations to leave no saved project, and require overwrite/duplicate semantics later in the flow. As written, a user can consume the save path before a successful generation, and failures can leave orphaned partial project assets. Define an explicit draft/temp session model or delay project creation until first save, move the 5-project quota check to create/duplicate save only, and specify cleanup/retention for failed or abandoned drafts.

findings.title: Final params editing and persistence are not designed
findings.detail: The spec requires `final_params` to be stored separately from `llm_result`, restored on reload, and used for regeneration with modified masks or params. The design/tasks only expose `animation_type` override (`6.12`) and never define UI/state/API work for editing `speed`, `amplitude`, `emphasis`, or `loop`. Without that, `final_params` will either be missing or just mirror the LLM output, and the reload/regenerate contract is incomplete. Add explicit tasks and data flow for reviewing/editing params before generate/regenerate, persisting them as `final_params`, and preserving the original `llm_result.params` unchanged.

findings.title: Empty-region fallback threshold changes the accepted contract
findings.detail: The spec says degraded fallback applies when a required region mask is empty. The design risk note and task `6.13` instead use `opaque pixel count < 10` as the trigger. That will misclassify legitimate tiny masks (especially small mouths/fins in pixel art) as empty, causing incorrect warnings and degraded rendering. Use exact zero-pixel emptiness for the fallback contract; if needed, add a separate advisory warning for unusually small regions without changing renderer behavior.

findings.title: Paid-plan quota is still unresolved even though design must finalize it
findings.detail: The spec explicitly says paid-plan quota numbers must be finalized in design, but the design leaves them as an open question and the tasks never encode the expanded limits. That leaves billing, quota checks, UI messaging, and tests (`10.8`, `10.11`, `14.4`) underspecified. Finalize the paid generation/save limits in the design and thread those constants through quota helpers, billing UI, webhook effects, and acceptance tests.

findings.title: The LLM parse result is never connected to the draft lifecycle
findings.detail: Upload creates a draft and routes to the mask screen, and a standalone `/api/llm/parse` route exists, but there is no task that actually invokes parsing after upload, persists `llm_result` onto the draft, or seeds `final_animation_type` / `final_params` from that result. As written, task 6.12 cannot reliably render the LLM result, task 8.3 cannot populate `project.json.llm_result`, and reload/regenerate lose the original parse. Add an explicit post-upload parse flow keyed by `draft_id` that stores `llm_result` plus initial `final_*` values and defines parse-failure handling.

findings.title: `final_params` are redesigned with incompatible value types
findings.detail: The spec fixes the parameter contract to `speed`=`slow|medium`, `amplitude`=`small|medium`, `emphasis`=`none|tail|mouth|fin`, and `loop`=boolean. D9.1 instead turns these into numeric sliders and a numeric loop count, and task 6.12 follows that model. If implemented, `final_params` will no longer match the fixed schema that the LLM returns or the project reproducibility contract. Keep `final_params` in the same four-key/value vocabulary and map those enum/boolean values to internal numeric coefficients inside the renderer rather than changing the persisted contract.

findings.title: Regeneration is still counted against the monthly generation quota
findings.detail: The proposal explicitly says regenerations do not consume the free-tier generation quota, but D6 and tasks 8.2, 8.4, and 11.5 apply the same quota check and `counted=true` insert to every `/api/generate` success, including regenerate flows rehydrated from an existing project. That will exhaust quotas incorrectly for the core reload/edit/regenerate loop. Distinguish first-time generation from regeneration and persist regenerated runs with `counted=false` so only initial successful generations count toward the monthly cap.

findings.title: Saving a draft does not rewrite `project.json` for the final saved project
findings.detail: Task 8.3 writes `project.json` under `{user_id}/drafts/{draft_id}/`, then tasks 9.3, 9.3.1, and 9.4 only move or copy artifacts during `new`, `overwrite`, and `duplicate` saves. There is no step to rebuild or patch `project.json` with the final `source_image_path`, `mask_image_path`, output paths, and correct `created_at`/`updated_at` for the saved project. That leaves saved metadata pointing at stale draft paths or stale timestamps after promotion or duplication. Either emit `project.json` only during save, or add an explicit rewrite step for every save mode before storing the final copy.

findings.title: `project.json` schema no longer matches the saved-project contract
findings.detail: The spec requires top-level `source_image_path`, `mask_image_path`, and an `outputs` object, but D6.1 and task 9.1 redefine the contract as `source_path`, `mask_path`, `gif_path`, and `spritesheet_path`. Implementing this will write incompatible `project.json` files and violate the exact-key reproducibility requirement. Update the design, serializer, and tests to emit the spec's exact top-level schema.

findings.title: Empty required-region generation is still blocked instead of degraded
findings.detail: Task 6.13 says to block generation submit when any required region has zero pixels, but the spec requires generation to proceed with a warning and renderer-side body-only fallback. Keeping the block makes the degraded-mode acceptance criteria unreachable. Replace the zero-pixel case with a non-blocking warning and let task 7.9 handle the fallback.

findings.title: LLM parse failure path contradicts the spec's rejection behavior
findings.detail: Tasks 4.8.1, 4.9, and 5.7 keep the draft/source image and route the user into manual editing when upload-time parsing fails or returns invalid output. The parsing spec says invalid LLM output must be rejected and no project data created. At minimum, schema-invalid responses need to roll back the draft/source and stop the flow; if manual fallback is desired, it needs an explicit spec change because it is a different product contract.

findings.title: `loop` is effectively fixed to true even though the contract requires a real boolean
findings.detail: D9.1 and task 6.12 describe the loop control as disabled and fixed on in MVP, but the spec requires `params.loop` to remain a boolean and the renderer to produce a single-play GIF when it is false. As written, a parsed or reloaded `loop=false` value cannot be reliably preserved into `final_params`. Keep `loop` as a true boolean end-to-end; if the UI is read-only, it must still display and retain `false` rather than coercing it to `true`.

findings.title: The proposed time-based indexes are not deployable as written
findings.detail: The schema in D5/D6.1 uses time-dependent expressions inside indexes (`updated_at < now() - interval '24 hours'`, and monthly bucketing on `date_trunc(..., created_at)`). Those expressions are not safe immutable index keys for Postgres and can prevent `0001_init.sql` from applying cleanly, which directly conflicts with task 2.6. Redesign these as ordinary indexes such as `(user_id, created_at)` / `(updated_at)` and perform month-window or cleanup filtering in queries or via an immutable generated column.

findings.title: Middleware coverage omits newly introduced authenticated routes
findings.detail: D7/task 3.2 only protect `/upload`, `/projects`, and `/api/*`, but the task set also introduces `/drafts/[draft_id]/mask` and `/billing`. The auth requirement says unauthenticated users should only see the landing/login surfaces, so these routes also need middleware protection and redirect behavior.

findings.title: UTC handling is still not pinned for quota resets and saved timestamps
findings.detail: The spec requires generation quotas to reset at the start of each UTC month and `project.json.created_at` / `updated_at` to be ISO8601 UTC timestamps. D5/D6.1 and tasks 11.2/9.1 still describe this in terms of generic `now()` / `date_trunc('month', now())` timestamps, which leaves the implementation free to depend on database/session timezone and to emit offset timestamps. Specify UTC-normalized month boundaries in the quota helper, require UTC serialization in the project.json serializer, and add tests that fail on non-UTC behavior.

findings.title: Reloading a saved project still does not explicitly restore prior outputs into the editor
findings.detail: The persistence spec says reopening a project must restore the previously generated outputs into the editor along with the source image, mask, prompt, LLM result, and final params. Tasks 6.2 and 9.7 only hydrate editor state for the source, mask, `llmResult`, and `final*` fields; 9.4.2 copies `gif` and `spritesheet` into the draft, but there is no task to load or display those outputs on `/drafts/[draft_id]/mask`. Add explicit editor-state/UI work so reopened drafts surface the existing GIF and spritesheet before regeneration.

findings.title: Billing return pages are left outside the authenticated-route contract
findings.detail: Task 3.2 protects `/billing` but not `/billing/*`, while task 10.4 adds `/billing/success` and `/billing/cancel`. The auth spec says unauthenticated users should only reach the landing/login surfaces, so these new billing routes need the same middleware protection or an intentional redirect flow through authenticated surfaces. As written, the route plan still leaves spec-external pages reachable without a session.
